tools.name: scalingo_list_apps
tools.description: List all Scalingo apps you can access in the current region. Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps. Returns { apps: [...] }.

tools.name: scalingo_get_app
tools.description: Fetch a single app's details (region, stack, status, URLs, flags). Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}. Returns { app }.

tools.name: scalingo_list_containers
tools.description: List an app's container formation — the running process types with their amount and size (the current scaling). Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/containers. Returns { containers: [{ name, amount, size }] }.

tools.name: scalingo_get_app_stats
tools.description: Real-time per-container resource stats (CPU / memory / swap usage) for an app. Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/stats. Returns { stats: [...] }.

tools.name: scalingo_list_deployments
tools.description: List an app's deployments (most recent first), paginated. Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/deployments. Returns { deployments: [...], meta: { pagination } }.

tools.name: scalingo_get_deployment
tools.description: Fetch a single deployment's details (status, git_ref, pusher, image size, timestamps). Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/deployments/{deployment_id}. Returns { deployment }.

tools.name: scalingo_get_app_logs
tools.description: Fetch recent application log lines. Scalingo returns an authenticated logs_url (GET /v1/apps/{app}/logs → { logs_url }); this tool then downloads the last N lines from it (dump mode) and returns them as text. Returns { logs_url, lines }. If the follow-up download fails, only logs_url is returned so

tools.name: scalingo_list_variables
tools.description: List an app's environment variables. WARNING: this exposes secret VALUES (API keys, database URLs, etc.). Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/variables. Returns { variables: [{ id, name, value }] }.

tools.name: scalingo_list_collaborators
tools.description: List an app's collaborators (users invited to the app) and their status. Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/collaborators. Returns { collaborators: [...] }.

tools.name: scalingo_list_domains
tools.description: List an app's custom domains and their TLS/canonical status. Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/domains. Returns { domains: [...] }.

tools.name: scalingo_list_addons
tools.description: List the addons (databases, services) provisioned on an app. Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/addons. Returns { addons: [...] }.

tools.name: scalingo_list_addon_providers
tools.description: List the addon providers available on Scalingo (databases, monitoring, etc.) with their plans embedded. Scalingo API: GET /v1/addon_providers. Returns { addon_providers: [{ ..., plans: [...] }] }.

tools.name: scalingo_list_app_events
tools.description: List an app's activity events (deployments, scaling, restarts, collaborator changes, etc.), paginated. Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/events. Returns { events: [...], meta: { pagination } }.

tools.name: scalingo_get_operation
tools.description: Poll the status of an asynchronous operation (e.g. a scale or restart returns an operation to track). Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/operations/{operation_id}. Returns { operation } with status pending|running|done|error.

tools.name: scalingo_list_regions
tools.description: List the Scalingo regions available to your account, each with its API/dashboard/database hosts. Useful to discover the right SCALINGO_REGION. Scalingo API: GET (auth host) /v1/regions. Returns { regions: [...] }.

tools.name: scalingo_get_account
tools.description: Fetch the authenticated user's account (id, email, username, fullname, company). Scalingo API: GET /v1/users/self. Returns { user }.

tools.name: scalingo_request
tools.description: Power-user escape hatch: GET any Scalingo API path not wrapped by a dedicated tool. READ-ONLY — only GET is allowed. Path is taken after /v1 (e.g. "/apps/my-app/alerts"). By default hits the regional API; set on_auth_host:true for auth-host resources (regions, scm_integrations, tokens). Scalingo API

tools.name: scalingo_restart_app
tools.description: MUTATES Scalingo infrastructure — restarts an app's containers. Optionally restart only specific process types via scope; omit scope to restart everything. Returns 202 Accepted (track via scalingo_get_operation). Scalingo API: POST /v1/apps/{app}/restart.

tools.name: scalingo_scale_app
tools.description: MUTATES Scalingo infrastructure — sets the container formation (number and/or size of each process type). Only the container types you include are changed. Returns 202 Accepted (track via scalingo_get_operation). Scalingo API: POST /v1/apps/{app}/scale.

tools.name: scalingo_set_variables
tools.description: MUTATES Scalingo infrastructure — creates or updates environment variables in bulk (each { name, value } is created if new or updated if it exists). This usually triggers a restart to apply the new env. Names ≤64 chars, values ≤8192 chars. Scalingo API: PUT /v1/apps/{app}/variables. Returns { variab

tools.name: scalingo_trigger_deployment
tools.description: MUTATES Scalingo infrastructure — triggers a new deployment from a source archive URL (a tar.gz reachable by Scalingo). To roll back, re-deploy a previous git_ref/archive — there is no separate rollback endpoint. Scalingo API: POST /v1/apps/{app}/deployments. Returns { deployment }.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: scalingo_get_app, scalingo_list_variables, scalingo_get_account · Private data: scalingo_list_variables, scalingo_list_regions, scalingo_request, scalingo_set_variables · Public sink: scalingo_get_account, scalingo_restart_app, scalingo_scale_app, scalingo_trigger_deployment.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: scalingo_get_app, scalingo_list_variables, scalingo_get_account · Private data: scalingo_list_variables, scalingo_list_regions, scalingo_request, scalingo_set_variables · Public sink: scalingo_get_account, scalingo_restart_app, scalingo_scale_app, scalingo_trigger_deployment

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
